messages:
ana: Heads-up — CloudNine SI reported a delayed hourly usage batch (~6h lag). Entitlements didn't roll forward for some customers and we got a few 'quota exhausted' escalations. Need an ops + partner playbook. Who's on this?

billing-bot: [ALERT] partner_delayed_batch - partner=cloudnine last_received=2026-03-20T19:12:07Z batch_window=hourly

devon: On it. Do we know if they're sending hourly windows or minute-level events aggregated upstream? Any sample payload would help.

samir: quick look at the raw logs shows window_end in local TZ (no Z). That's probably the root cause — our hourly rollup expects Zulu timestamps. Example (from their webhook):
```json
{
  "customer_id": "c_84f9",
  "usage_units": 12500,
  "unit_type": "tokens",
  "window_end": "2026-03-20T18:00",
  "event_uuid": "b4c2-..."
}
```

ana: (typo; assume ana) ana: we require ISO8601 with timezone or epoch seconds. If partner sends naive local timestamps ingestion sometimes picks previous window -> late detection fails.

maria: Partnership question: what's the expected partner-facing message? Customers are already annoyed. We need a short comms template and an SLA ask for them to fix timestamp formatting and include event UUIDs.

devon: Proposed immediate mitigation + playbook:
1) Accept naive timestamps as backfill if `event_uuid` present and `event_time` can be disambiguated via partner's timezone header. Mark as `backfill:true`.
2) Run idempotent backfill job for affected windows (48h window). Command we ran locally: `./tools/run-backfill --partner cloudnine --from 2026-03-20T00:00Z --to 2026-03-20T19:00Z --rate 200/s`
3) Apply credits if any customer saw overquota charge due to late ingestion.
4) Push patch to webhook verifier that rejects naive timestamps without a `X-Partner-TZ` header and return `422` after a 24h grace period.

ben: +1 but throttle the backfill. Last backfill spike caused secondary index contention. Suggest `--rate 75/s` and `--concurrency 4`. Also set DB write batch size to 500.

samir: I'll open a small PR to the webhook verifier and add a unit test for naive vs zulu timestamps. Also adding a quick harness script for partners: `scripts/emit-sample --tz Europe/London` so they can test.

maria: For partner comms: draft snippet — "We observed delayed usage batches that used timezone-naive timestamps. This caused entitlement reconciliation delays. We're performing a backfill and will send credits if impacted. Please update your webhook to include timezone (RFC3339) or send epoch seconds." Can someone turn that into a one-paragraph email and an ops checklist?

devon: I'll post the ops checklist to the runbook and kick off the backfill now. ETA ~2-3h with throttling. Will update with job id and progress.

billing-bot: Backfill job started - job_id=jb_20260320_cn_01 initiated_by=devon

ana: (typo again) ana: I'll own the partner note and loop legal + CS for credits. @devon please paste job_id here when available and include a small csv of affected accounts for CS to reach out.

devon: job_id=jb_20260320_cn_01. Attaching summary CSV to internal ticket. Updating runbook now: https://confluence.redwood/partnerships/cloudnine-backfill-playbook

maria: Thanks all. After this stabilizes let's schedule a short integration bugfix call with CloudNine engineering tomorrow to nail down timezone header and add end-to-end test. :thumbsup:

samir: I'll also add a synthetic test to our CI that simulates naive timestamps and ensures backfill path marks `backfill:true` and doesn't double-count. PR coming in ~30m.

ben: Monitoring note — set a temporary alert: `ingest.backfill_rate > 100/s` to catch runaway jobs. I'll add it.

ana: Great. Keeping thread for updates.
